record.name: Schwarzwald Dry Gin
record.description: A Black Forest dry gin with 47 declared botanicals. A partial, source-linked ingredient inventory; no reconstructed secret formula.
record.history: In a published founder interview, Alexander Stein places the start of the project in 2008, before the scale of the gin revival was apparent. His account emphasizes making a distinctive product with limited initial resources rather than treating craft as a new invention. The gin connects the Black Forest’s fruit-distilling culture and botanical landscape with the British gin tradition. Its apothecary-style bottle and numbered identity make that mixture of laboratory, landscape and storytelling visible. The 47-botanical declaration is preserved as a producer claim; it does not reveal the proportions or establish a special neurological effect.

record.description: A source-linked entry in the Suntory range. Bottling specifications and ingredient membership require edition-specific verification.
record.history: Shinjiro Torii founded Torii Shoten in Osaka in 1899. Construction of Yamazaki began in 1923; Hakushu followed in 1973. The house developed several identities around blending, place and Japanese craft: Kakubin appeared in 1937 and Hibiki in 1989. This bottle belongs to that evolving portfolio, rather than representing a separate distillery in every case.

record.title: Nutmeg metabolite analysis
record.finding: Measured metabolites did not establish the proposed amphetamine derivatives.
record.limitation: Not a gin study; does not quantify exposure from any catalogue product.

record.title: Lavender oil abuse-potential trial
record.finding: Standardized lavender oil was similar to placebo on drug-liking and did not show sedative effects in this trial.
record.limitation: Oil preparation rather than pure linalool or gin; no alcohol co-administration inference.

record.title: Acute lemon balm and stress
record.finding: A standardized extract increased self-rated calmness and reduced alertness at the higher studied dose.
record.limitation: Small trial of an oral extract; no proof that active constituents transfer to distilled spirits.

record.title: Thujone with matched alcohol
record.finding: High-thujone condition affected attention and temporarily counteracted alcohol-related anxiety reduction.
record.limitation: Not Monkey 47; effects depended on concentration; no evidence of a mushroom-like effect.

record.title: Beta-caryophyllene receptor study
record.finding: Selective functional CB2 agonism and anti-inflammatory effects were observed.
record.limitation: Preclinical findings; nonpsychotropic CB2 activity is not evidence of THC-like intoxication.

record.title: Ethanol and NMDA ion currents
record.finding: Ethanol inhibited NMDA-activated currents in a concentration-dependent manner.
record.limitation: Cellular experiment, not an individualized brain simulation or a product-specific comparison.

record.title: Linalool odour and anxiety-like behaviour
record.finding: Odour exposure reduced anxiety-like behaviours; effects required olfaction and were blocked by flumazenil.
record.limitation: Animal inhalation experiment. No gin exposure or human intoxication conclusion.

record.title: Odour exposure and stress responses
record.finding: Certain odour groups showed changes in anxiety ratings and physiological measures.
record.limitation: Small inhalation study, not drinking, not a demonstration of a cannabinoid high.

record.title: Chamomile extract for generalized anxiety
record.finding: The trial suggested modest improvement in anxiety scores with oral chamomile extract.
record.limitation: Chronic extract administration; not evidence of acute intoxication or activity in gin.
One documented target among many; no regional brain activation or dose-response prediction is visualized.
Not proof of direct receptor binding, human effects or exposure from a bottle.
CB2 activity is not equivalent to THC-like CB1 intoxication.

record.action: May oppose some alcohol-related effects at high exposure
record.limitation: No thujone measurement in catalogue bottles; cannot infer a product effect.
